story:
Caisha is a face kept in water. She stands in no hall and holds no line on the Roll; the court lists her, when it lists her at all, among the furnishings of Princess Nahemah's room, and the furnishing she belongs to is the well. She is a mortal, or was. Her shape is the shape of the soultorn, the torn souls of soldiers that wander the hollow, but she is smaller than most of them and older than all of them, because she was taken long before the doors opened, when nothing mortal came into the court except by mischance.

The three realms each claim her, and none agree. Albion's Church says she was a lady of the old kings' household who walked in the castle ruins of Camelot Hills, where the Albion door now stands, and heard singing under the stones. Hibernia's druids say she was a girl of Connacht who went into a green hill on Samhain eve and came out on the wrong side of it; Tir na Nog still names her as one of its own, and the name Caisha comes from there, if it is her name. Midgard's skalds do not know who she was and call her the girl in the well. The bower, when asked, says that what she was does not matter, only what she is for.

What she is for is her face. The princess's household wears what mortals want and trust, and a face is easiest to wear when its owner is kept close and kept fresh. Nahemah drowned the girl's soul in the well of her own room so that it would not age, and has drawn the face up out of the water whenever the bower had need of it. When Ambassador Mannam went up the Albion stair to the king's hall, it was Caisha's face he wore, folded in a dark stone at his belt, and the Church of Albion has never forgiven itself for letting it in.

The princess's women say the girl never leaves the rim of the well, and has stood there so long that she no longer knows she could. They are careful in that room: they keep it quiet and keep the water covered, and they do not go near the rim. Mystemas, who wants the princess and the ambassador dead and has said so to anyone who will listen, wants Caisha as well, and offers the realms a stone to catch her in. He says it is a kindness to the girl. The bower says it is theft, and that the imp means to wear her himself. Hibernia's bards, who sing of her at wakes, say only that she has waited a long time at the bottom of the water for someone to come for her, and that she has no reason to think the next one will be kinder than the last.
legend: Caisha stands by the well in Princess Nahemah's room, about thirteen hundred units from the princess. The Hibernian quest text says she rises from the well when the princess dies; in this world she is simply there, a permanent spawn that comes back in about three minutes. Level 50, a soultorn spirit, no script, not hard. Do not let a fight with the princess drift over to the well, or you will have her too. Hibernia's version of the quest catches her spirit in Mystemas's soul stone; Albion and Midgard never meet her and take the stone from Ambassador Mannam instead. Players say she is the face the ambassador wore at Camelot. Hibernians call her one of their own, and a few will not finish the quest out of pity. Most do, because the reward is good.

loremasterTopic.text: A drowned mortal soul kept in the well of Princess [Nahemah]'s room so that her face would not age. Ambassador [Mannam] wore it at Albion's throne. She rises when the princess falls. Albion and Hibernia both claim her; Midgard calls her the girl in the well.

bookPage: From The Girl in the Well, as the bards of Tir na Nog sing it at wakes, set down in prose: She went into the green hill on the eve of Samhain to follow the music, and the music was sweet, and she came out on the wrong side of the hill, under the world, in a room that smelled of perfume and storm. There was a well in the room and a lady beside it. The lady said she had a beautiful face, and asked to borrow it, and the girl said yes, because she was polite. That is the whole of her fault. The lady put her in the water so the face would keep.
